dataset.description: The expert survey aims to investigate the ecological and environmental impacts of beaver activity on river ecosystems, alongside the effects of river cleanup efforts. The data gathered will provide valuable insights into the causes and motives behind these activities, with a particular focus on understanding why experts often view beaver impacts negatively. By collecting and analyzing perspectives from environmental scientists, ecologists, and conservationists, this research will contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of the interplay between beaver populations and river health. The plan details the methods for data collection, storage, sharing, and preservation, ensuring that the research data remains reliable and accessible for future use.

distribution.title: The purpose of this data collection is to gather expert insights on the ecological and environmental impacts of beaver activity within river ecosystems, particularly in relation to ongoing river cleanup efforts. This data is crucial for understanding the underlying causes and motivations for these activities, as well as addressing the predominantly negative perceptions of beaver impacts among experts. The data will originate from structured surveys and interviews with environmental scientists, ecologists, and conservationists who have direct experience or knowledge of the subject matter. This information will support the broader objectives of the “Water Cultures” project by contributing to a more comprehensive understanding of the interplay between human activities, wildlife, and river health, ultimately informing sustainable management practices.

dataset.title: Expert survey on the ecological and environmental impact of beaver activity and river cleanup efforts

dataset.description:
Online survey aims to identify the key meanings, values, preferences and concerns related to rivers in the context of recreation and water tourism. Online survey will provide an insight into the motivations, expectations, imaginaries and preferences that underlie the recreational engagements with water environments and riverscapes in Latvia. 
The online survey will be distributed in various online media platforms (websites of municipalities, oganizations for local and regional tourism promotion, thematically related social groups on the social media networks (e.g. Facebook)). 
The data will represent insights and perspectives of people with a diverse range of experiences of recreational boating. 
The data will be used to analyze how recreational engagements with water environments and riverscapes reflect broader cultural tendencies of human-water relationships in Latvia.

distribution.title: Online survey is used to identify individual and collective values, meanings and preferences regarding water, water environments and riverscapes in Latvia among a specific group of social actors – water tourists.

dataset.title: Online survey on social meanings of rivers in Latvia among the practitioners of water tourism

dmp.description:
The primary purposes of the DMP are:

1. The DMP provides clear guidelines for systematically collecting and integrating empirical data across various case studies. This ensures that all data, whether qualitative or quantitative, is consistently recorded and made interoperable.
2. The DMP outlines procedures for handling data with respect to privacy and cultural significance, particularly when dealing with sensitive cultural information and practices.
3. Given the sensitive nature of the data, the DMP defines strict conditions for access and sharing. Access to data will be carefully controlled and limited to authorized project stakeholders, ensuring that it is used responsibly and remains protected.
4. The DMP establishes protocols for preserving data long-term, including strategies for migrating data to sustainable repositories if needed, ensuring accessibility beyond the project’s lifespan, within the limits of the established restrictions.
5. While the data is restricted, the DMP ensures that it is preserved in a way that allows it to support future research, policy development, and educational purposes where appropriate, contributing to sustainable water management practices.

By providing a structured approach to data management, the DMP plays a crucial role in ensuring that the insights gained from the “Water Cultures” project are preserved, shared, and utilized to their fullest potential, contributing to the development of sustainable human-water relations in Latvia and beyond.
dmp.ethical_issues_description: There are ethical considerations related to the privacy and confidentiality of the experts providing survey responses. The data collection involves personal opinions and potentially sensitive information regarding environmental practices, which must be handled with care to protect the identities and integrity of the participants. Legal considerations include compliance with data protection regulations, such as GDPR, ensuring that all data is collected, stored, and processed in a way that respects participants’ rights. The project will adhere to strict ethical guidelines and will seek approval from the appropriate ethics committee to ensure all data handling practices are in full compliance with legal and ethical standards.

project.title: Water cultures: transformative approach for sustainable human-water relations (lzp-2023/1-0248)
